title: Priority Re-Admission Workflow for Churn-risk Accounts After Critical Incidents
creator: Aisha Kaur
description:
Problem: Several enterprise customers that experienced critical incidents (regional SLA breaches or data access interruptions) are at elevated churn risk. Current intake for prioritized roadmap asks is optimized for feature requests, not for re-admitting accounts after incidents. We need a repeatable, fast-track re-admission and runway process that: 1) accepts a scoped set of commitments (short-term mitigations + timeline), 2) reserves engineering runway and dedicated success contact for the account, and 3) surfaces rollback/fallback policies to protect platform SLAs.

Goal: Create a Priority Re-Admission Workflow that reduces time-to-commit for escalated accounts to <= 10 business days, ties commitments to measurable deliverables, and standardizes the intake so PM, Eng, Solutions, and Legal can make decisions rapidly.

Acceptance criteria:
- Intake form + triage rubric that consistently classifies incident severity, business impact, and commitment tier.
- SLO for decision-to-commit within 5 business days and delivery runway planning within 10 business days for Tier A accounts.
- Template commitment letters (scoped deliverables, timelines, rollback/fallback options) stored in Drive and referenced by Sales/CS.
- Engineering slot reservation process with clear cancellation/fallback rules and cost bucket tagging for Dedicated/Private customers.
- Dashboard widget in Console showing active re-admission commitments and their delivery status.

Proposed solution in brief:
- 1) Build a "Re-Admission" intake route in the customer portal and internal intake board that tags requests as "incident-recovery" and assigns a priority score.
- 2) Triage rubric maintained by Solutions + PM that outputs: commitment tier (monitor-only, config fix, feature patch, custom integration), estimated effort band, and risk score.
- 3) Pre-approved commitment templates (legal-light) for low-risk scopes and escalation legal review for high-risk scopes.
- 4) Engineering runway reservation: a lightweight reserve API that marks timeboxed capacity on Dedicated pools and flags required quantization/kernel work for runtime.
- 5) Operational dashboard in Console to monitor commitments and auto-escalate breaches to exec sponsor.

Trade-offs considered:
- Fast-track vs. quality: We accept short-lived, tightly scoped commitments (1-2 sprints) with explicit rollback to avoid long-term product divergence.
- Capacity reservation granularity: reserving fractional GPU time adds scheduler complexity; instead we propose fixed timeboxes to reduce runtime changes.
- Legal pre-approval reduces friction but increases risk surface; we keep a tiered approach to minimize legal overhead.
